context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within EU infrastructure. It ensures high-performance search capabilities and secure external integrations while maintaining strict EU-only data residency.

## Key Elements
- **Library Patrons:** End-users accessing public catalogs and self-service portals.
- **Library Staff:** Administrative users managing cataloging and circulation.
- **Library Management System:** Core software system handling business logic and data.
- **External Payment Gateway:** Third-party system for processing fines and fees.
- **Digital Content Repositories:** External systems for streaming and downloading digital items.

## Relationships
- **Patrons & Staff to Library Management System:** HTTPS/TLS 1.3 via dedicated Patron Self-Service and Staff Management interfaces.
- **Library Management System to External Payment Gateway:** mTLS over HTTPS for secure financial transactions.
- **Library Management System to Digital Content Repositories:** mTLS over HTTPS with OpenID Connect (OIDC) SSO handoffs.

## Technology Stack
- **EU-Region Cloud Infrastructure:** Mandated to strictly satisfy EU-only data residency and GDPR constraints.
- **TLS 1.3 & mTLS:** Utilized for all client-to-system and machine-to-machine communications to ensure data security in transit.
- **OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.1:** Implemented for federated authentication, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and seamless SSO integration.
- **AES-256:** Deployed for robust data encryption at rest within EU boundaries.
- **Edge WAF & Rate Limiting:** Deployed at the Patron interface to protect against volumetric spikes and meet the search performance requirement.

## Rationale
Separating the Patron and Staff ingress points structurally isolates high-throughput public searches from resource-heavy administrative batch tasks, safeguarding the p99 < 800ms search latency requirement. Enforcing strict EU-only cloud deployment, mTLS boundaries, and Zero Trust security controls ensures full compliance with data residency and privacy mandates.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The Library Management System is a comprehensive digital platform for public and academic libraries designed to catalogue physical and digital assets, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals.]
[It strictly enforces EU-only data residency and maintains a 99th-percentile search response time of under 800 milliseconds.]

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
* External Payment Gateway and Digital Content Repositories (External Systems)
* Web Application (React/TypeScript, Nginx)
* API Gateway (Kong or Spring Cloud Gateway)
* Core Domain Service (Java/Spring Boot)
* Search Service (Python/FastAPI, Elasticsearch)
* Notification Service (Node.js)
* PostgreSQL Database
* RabbitMQ Message Broker

## Relationships
* Users to Web Application via HTTPS
* Web Application to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
* API Gateway to Core Domain Service and Search Service via gRPC with mTLS
* Core Domain Service to PostgreSQL via TLS 1.3
* Notification Service to RabbitMQ via AMQP with TLS 1.3
* External Systems to API Gateway via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* React/TypeScript & Nginx: Client-side rendering and static asset hosting
* Kong / Spring Cloud Gateway: API routing, rate limiting, and OAuth2/OIDC token validation
* Java / Spring Boot: Core business logic, circulation management, and immutable audit logging
* Python / FastAPI & Elasticsearch: High-performance search to meet the <800ms P99 requirement
* PostgreSQL: Relational operational data store with primary-replica streaming
* Node.js & RabbitMQ: Asynchronous messaging with quorum queues for zero-loss notifications
* Kubernetes: Container orchestration utilizing NetworkPolicies, PDBs, and HPAs in EU-region clusters

## Rationale
[The container decomposition isolates the high-performance search engine to meet strict latency goals while maintaining modular scalability for core circulation tasks.]
[A secure, Kubernetes-orchestrated, EU-hosted infrastructure guarantees strict regulatory data residency and zero-trust security compliance.]

Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. The architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons
- Library Staff
- Web Application (React, TypeScript, Nginx reverse proxy)
- API Gateway (Kong or Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Core Domain Service (Java, Spring Boot)
- Search Service (Python, FastAPI, Elasticsearch)
- Notification Service (Node.js)
- PostgreSQL Database
- RabbitMQ Message Broker
- External Payment Gateway
- Digital Content Repositories

## Relationships
- Library Patrons -> Web Application: Accesses public catalogs and self-service portals [HTTPS]
- Library Staff -> Web Application: Manages cataloging and circulation [HTTPS]
- Web Application -> API Gateway: Routes API requests via Nginx reverse proxy [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Core Domain Service, Search Service, Notification Service [gRPC/REST]
- Search Service -> Elasticsearch [TCP]
- Core Domain Service -> PostgreSQL Database [JDBC/TLS]
- Core Domain Service -> RabbitMQ Message Broker [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript with Nginx: Client-side rendering, static asset hosting, and secure reverse proxy/BFF pattern for session management.
- Java/Spring Boot: Powers the robust Core Domain Service for complex business logic.
- Python/FastAPI & Elasticsearch: Delivers high-performance search capabilities meeting sub-800ms latency requirements.
- PostgreSQL & RabbitMQ: Provides reliable relational data storage and asynchronous messaging.
- TLS 1.3 & HttpOnly Cookies: Secures data-in-transit and protects session tokens from XSS.

## Rationale
This architecture combines a high-performance frontend with a scalable microservices backend to meet stringent sub-800ms search SLAs. Furthermore, utilizing Nginx as a reverse proxy for secure cookie handling ensures strict compliance with EU-only data residency mandates.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[A secure, high-performance API Gateway built on Kong for the Library Management System, providing edge routing, security enforcement, and observability for public and academic library portals.]

## Key Elements
- **Routing Engine (Kong Proxy)**: Handles API versioning, priority routing for Library Staff, and downstream traffic direction.
- **Authentication Filter (Kong OIDC Plugin)**: Performs local JWT/OIDC token validation at the edge.
- **Rate Limiting & Circuit Breaker**: Protects downstream services and enforces throttling on search/auth endpoints.
- **Security & Telemetry Enforcers**: Injects security headers, sanitizes inputs, and emits OpenTelemetry/Prometheus metrics.

## Relationships
- **Web Application -> Routing Engine**: Forwards versioned client requests [HTTPS/REST using TLS 1.3]
- **Routing Engine -> Core Domain Service & Search Service**: Proxies validated traffic [gRPC with mTLS]
- **Routing Engine -> Telemetry Exporter**: Emits distributed traces and Prometheus metrics [Internal]

## Technology Stack
- **Kong API Gateway**: Selected for its robust plugin ecosystem and low-latency edge processing.
- **DB-less Kubernetes Mode**: Eliminates stateful database dependencies at the edge to support EU data residency and GitOps.
- **gRPC with mTLS**: Ensures secure, high-performance service-to-service communication.
- **OpenTelemetry & Prometheus**: Enables distributed tracing to meet the <800ms search SLA.

## Rationale
[The DB-less Kong architecture eliminates external edge latency while enforcing strict EU data residency compliance. Furthermore, priority routing, local JWT validation, and gRPC/mTLS guarantee rapid, secure self-service portal performance.]

Core Domain Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Domain Service provides business logic, circulation management, and EU-compliant audit logging for the Library Management System. It handles item cataloguing, loan policies, and secure self-service portal operations.

## Key Elements
- **Core Domain Service** (Container, Java/Spring Boot)
- **Circulation Manager Component** (Spring Bean/Service)
- **Catalogue Manager Component** (Spring Bean/Service)
- **Audit Logger Component** (Spring Bean/Data JPA)
- **Event Publisher Component** (Spring Cloud Stream / RabbitMQ Template)
- **Security Interceptor Component** (Spring Security / gRPC Interceptor)
- **PostgreSQL Database** (Container, PostgreSQL with dedicated audit schema)
- **RabbitMQ Message Broker** (Container, RabbitMQ with DLQ)

## Relationships
- `API Gateway` -> `Security Interceptor Component`: Forwards requests [gRPC with mTLS]
- `Security Interceptor` -> `Circulation Manager` & `Catalogue Manager`: Authorizes validated gRPC calls
- `Core Domain Service components` -> `PostgreSQL Database`: Persists transactional state [JDBC over TLS 1.3]
- `Audit Logger` -> `PostgreSQL Database`: Writes to a restricted, append-only schema [JDBC over TLS 1.3]
- `Core Domain Service` -> `RabbitMQ Message Broker`: Publishes domain events like `ItemCheckedOut` [AMQP 0-9-1 over TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **Java / Spring Boot**: Enforces strict domain boundaries and transaction management.
- **Spring Security / gRPC Interceptor**: Validates method-level OAuth2/JWT scopes for roles.
- **Spring Data JPA**: Manages database persistence and object-relational mapping.
- **PostgreSQL**: Stores operational data and isolated, immutable audit logs.
- **RabbitMQ**: Handles asynchronous domain event dispatching with circuit breakers and dead-letter queues.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates the immutable audit logger into a dedicated database schema with least-privilege permissions, ensuring strict EU data residency and GDPR compliance. Furthermore, bounded thread pools and mTLS protect core circulation performance and transaction reliability.

Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Search Service provides high-performance catalogue searching for the Library Management System, meeting strict sub-second response times and EU data residency constraints. It processes physical and digital item queries securely while supporting advanced ranking and facet filtering.

## Key Elements
- **API Gateway**: Kong or Spring Cloud Gateway forwarding requests via gRPC with mTLS.
- **Search Service Container**: Python/FastAPI runtime housing search components.
- **Search API Controller**: FastAPI endpoint validating JWT claims from gRPC metadata.
- **Query Pipeline Processor**: Combines query parsing, facet/filter processing, and the relevance/ranking engine.
- **Search Repository**: `elasticsearch-py` client executing queries against Elasticsearch.
- **Index Synchronizer**: Consumes domain events from RabbitMQ to maintain index freshness.
- **Caching Layer**: In-memory Redis cache with role-based cache key segregation.
- **Elasticsearch**: Dedicated data nodes with NVMe storage in an EU-only Kubernetes cluster.
- **RabbitMQ**: Message broker with AMQP protocol, TLS/SASL, and a dead-letter queue (DLQ).

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Search API Controller [gRPC with mTLS]
- Search API Controller -> Query Pipeline Processor [In-process]
- Query Pipeline Processor -> Search Repository [In-process / AsyncIO]
- Index Synchronizer -> Search Repository [In-process / AsyncIO]
- Index Synchronizer <- RabbitMQ Message Broker [AMQP with TLS/SASL]
- Search Repository -> Elasticsearch Cluster [Transport Layer Security with RBAC]

## Technology Stack
- **Python / FastAPI**: Chosen for asynchronous request handling and low-latency performance.
- **Elasticsearch**: Native sub-second P99 search performance over catalogued items.
- **RabbitMQ**: Asynchronous event consumption for search index synchronization.
- **Redis**: In-memory caching for frequent, non-personalized search optimization.
- **Kubernetes**: EU-only cluster deployment with Horizontal Pod Autoscalers.
- **OpenTelemetry**: Distributed tracing across gRPC boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture uses FastAPI and Elasticsearch to guarantee P99 search latency below 800ms under peak load. Strict EU Kubernetes placement, TLS encryption, and role-based access controls satisfy regional data residency and security mandates.

  - type: "component"

  - type: "component"

Notification Service.analysis:
## Overview
- Solution: Notification Service component within the Library Management System for asynchronous messaging and zero-loss patron notifications.
- Purpose: Delivers localized alerts via email and SMS while enforcing EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- AMQP Consumer Component (Node.js, amqplib)
- Notification Router Component (Node.js)
- Template Engine Component (Nunjucks)
- Provider Integration Adapters (Node.js, Axios, SendGrid, Twilio)
- Outbox Repository Component (Node.js, TypeORM, PostgreSQL)
- Preference Cache Component (Node.js, ioredis, Redis)

## Relationships
- AMQP Consumer -> RabbitMQ: Consumes event messages [AMQP 0-9-1 with TLS 1.3]
- Notification Router -> Preference Cache: Queries patron preferences [In-Memory/TCP]
- Notification Router -> Template Engine: Renders localized templates [Internal Call]
- Notification Router -> Provider Integration Adapters: Sends payload [HTTPS]
- Provider Integration Adapters -> Outbox Repository: Persists delivery status [SQL/TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js: Lightweight runtime for asynchronous messaging and IO-bound tasks
- RabbitMQ: Message broker with manual acknowledgments and dead-letter exchanges for zero-loss guarantees
- Nunjucks: Template engine supporting secure, localized message rendering
- PostgreSQL: Central database ensuring strict EU-only data residency and outbox audit logs
- Redis: In-memory cache for low-latency patron preference lookups
- SendGrid & Twilio: External providers for email and SMS delivery

## Rationale
- The architecture guarantees zero message loss and sub-second routing via decoupled consumers, outbox patterns, and low-latency caching.
- Compliance with EU data residency and privacy mandates is strictly maintained through encrypted PostgreSQL storage and secure in-transit protocols.

PostgreSQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals with strict EU data residency compliance. The PostgreSQL database architecture provides robust transactional storage, automated failover, and workload isolation to meet sub-800ms performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- PostgreSQL Storage: Relational database engine managing ACID transactions
- PgBouncer: Connection pooler preventing resource exhaustion
- Patroni with etcd: Consensus-based automated failover manager
- Read-Only Replica Router: Logical routing layer for administrative traffic
- PostgreSQL Read Replica: Asynchronous replica for reporting workloads
- Prometheus Exporter: Metrics sidecar for operational observability
- pgaudit: Audit logging extension for compliance monitoring

## Relationships
- Core Domain Service -> PgBouncer: SQL queries [TCP/IP over mTLS 1.3]
- PgBouncer -> PostgreSQL Storage: SQL queries [TCP/IP over mTLS 1.3]
- Library Staff -> Read-Only Replica Router: SQL queries [TCP/IP over TLS 1.3]
- Read-Only Replica Router -> PostgreSQL Replica: SQL queries [TCP/IP over mTLS 1.3]
- PostgreSQL Storage -> Volume Mount: Encrypted persistence [LUKS/AES-256]

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL: Core relational database for robust ACID transaction handling
- PgBouncer: Connection pooling to handle heavy concurrency and prevent exhaustion
- Patroni & etcd: High availability orchestration ensuring zero single points of failure
- LUKS/AES-256: Volume-level storage encryption ensuring EU data residency compliance
- Prometheus & Grafana: Telemetry and alerting stack monitoring replication lag and connection saturation
- pg_backrest / WAL-G: Point-in-time recovery targeting geo-redundant EU object storage

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency via encrypted storage while maintaining high availability and predictable sub-800ms response times for patrons. Isolating reporting traffic onto a read-only replica protects operational performance under heavy academic traffic.

RabbitMQ Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The RabbitMQ Message Broker provides asynchronous messaging and zero-loss notification processing for the Library Management System. It ensures high availability and reliable communication across core domain services under strict EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Exchange Router Component
- Quorum Queue Component
- Connection Manager Component
- Management API/UI Component
- Dead Letter Router Component
- Policy Enforcement Component

## Relationships
- Core Domain Service -> Connection Manager Component [AMQP 0-9-1 with TLS 1.3]
- Notification Service -> Connection Manager Component [AMQP 0-9-1 with TLS 1.3]
- Quorum Queue Component -> Dead Letter Router Component [AMQP 0-9-1]
- Management API/UI Component -> Monitoring Stack [HTTP/S over Port 15672]

## Technology Stack
- RabbitMQ: Core message broker technology chosen for robust AMQP support and quorum queues.
- Quorum Queues: Raft-consensus-backed storage ensuring zero-loss messaging.
- TLS 1.3 & mTLS: Encrypts data in transit and secures service authentication.
- Prometheus: Exports operational metrics for centralized observability.

## Rationale
This architecture uses clustered quorum queues and strict security controls to meet zero-loss messaging and EU data residency constraints. Resource guardrails and priority handling ensure high availability and performance during peak library loads.
